one_line_contribution: A pre-registered measurement of how much of a retrieved-experience memory bank's benefit is absorbed by an instruction that a reflective optimizer (GEPA) wrote from the same 800 training episodes, with the genuinely new instrument being the 'headroom curve' — a family of information-free instructions (H1 evidence-citation, H2 decompose-and-verify, I0+3 extra search budget) used to subtract off the ceiling effect that any accuracy-raising prompt would produce, so that the residual Delta_abs can be read as absorption rather than as a better baseline.
closest_prior_work: Two, and together they squeeze the contribution. (1) MIPROv2 (2406.11695): the instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint ablation on one training set IS the two-container question, and its recurring finding that the split is task-dependent already predicts the proposal's likely answer. The proposal's honest reply — retrieval, distillation, a held-out-episode crossover and token matching are added — is a delta of controls, not of question. (2) EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) as described: Vanilla / Memento / ReasoningBank / GEPA on shared 528/267 trajectories, and on Qwen3.5-27B — an in-scope candidate agent here — GEPA +1.2 vs ReasoningBank +3.6, with GEPA the strongest automatic method on Gemma-4-31B at +5.7. The qualitative headline 'a prompt optimizer on the same episodes gets you roughly what the memory bank gets you, on 27-31B models' is therefore already in the literature. What survives is narrower than the title implies: the combined cell I1xM_ab, the level-matched headroom control, the compiled block C_ab at matched tokens, and paired statistics. That is a worthwhile measurement paper but not a new claim about the world, and a reviewer who has read EvoAgentBench will say so.
strongest_objection: The primary confirmatory endpoint is not identified by the design that is supposed to identify it. Delta_abs = g_H(l1) - g(I1_ab, B_ab) requires that memory's gain depends on the instruction ONLY through the no-memory accuracy level — a one-dimensional headroom assumption anchored on three points, one of which (I0+3) is not an instruction at all but a tool-budget change, and which the proposal itself concedes may require extrapolating past the family's range because a 350-rollout GEPA instruction will plausibly outrun a one-line 'cite your evidence' prompt. Two prompts at equal no-memory accuracy can differ enormously in how usable retrieved items are (H2's decompose-and-verify reshapes the trajectory distribution; I0+3 changes it via search, not context), so a positive Delta_abs is equally consistent with 'GEPA wrote a better GENERIC procedural instruction than H1/H2' — nothing absorbed from any episode. The design's only probe that could discriminate this is Delta_info, and Falsifiable Prediction 2 pre-registers Delta_info within [-1,+1]pt in E1 and calls that outcome 'generic absorption, reported as such, not a failure.' That is circular: the mechanism probe is pre-declared to return the uninformative value, and the uninformative value is then read as confirmation. Compounding it, the planted control B_a+proc10 is written from gold documents and certifies sensitivity only to near-oracle half-specific items at ~15-30pt, not to the 1-2pt natural content whose absence the null is meant to license (Risk 12 admits this, then the interpretation rule ignores it). Second-order but real: the claim threshold is 2pt while the stated MDE is <=2.9pt and the measured treatment-free floor is ~2pt at n=1,500 — the headline effect is the size of the study's own noise.
what_would_fix_it: Four concrete changes, none of which require more than a modest budget increase. (1) Make the headroom family an actual curve: 5-6 information-free instructions chosen on S_dev2 to BRACKET acc(I1_ab x M0) from both sides, with the pre-registration forbidding extrapolation; and validate the one-dimensional assumption directly by showing that two family members at matched levels give matched g — if they do not, Delta_abs is not interpretable and the paper should say so before unblinding. (2) Add the bank re-distilled under the optimized instruction (see missing_baseline) so that Delta_abs is not confounded with trajectory-distribution mismatch. (3) Promote cell 12 (I1a x M0, I1b x M0) and cell 19 (I3 length control) from Tier 1 to Tier 0: the Tier-0 confirmatory family F-B is uninterpretable without per-half M0 levels (if neither own nor other bank beats M0 at I1a, Delta_info ~ 0 says nothing, planted control or not), and the whole content-vs-length story rests on I3, which the contingency order currently allows to be cut. (4) Make the confirmatory environment one with recurring procedural structure. Running the substitution test primarily in E1 (BM25 multi-hop QA over HotpotQA/MuSiQue/2Wiki) tests it where procedural memory is least likely to have anything to absorb; if memory is absorbable there, the memory community will answer that they never claimed gains there. E2 or a web/tool agent should carry the confirmatory result, with E1 as replication.
missing_baseline: A bank re-distilled from episodes generated UNDER the optimized instruction (call it B_ab | I1). As written, screening stage S1 generates the 800-episode training pool with bare I0, so every bank item is a lesson extracted from I0-shaped trajectories, and cell 3 then injects those items into an agent running I1_ab. If memory's gain shrinks at I1_ab, the most mundane explanation available to a reviewer is not absorption and not headroom but distribution mismatch: the bank's procedures no longer describe what the optimized agent does. I2_ab runs the opposite coupling (optimizer sees the bank) and does not cover this. Without B_ab | I1 the paper is auditing others for a confound of exactly the kind it leaves in its own primary cell. Secondary omission: a token-matched LONG hand-written instruction is only I3 at Tier 1 and is cuttable, yet the 'content not length' reading of Delta_abs depends on it.
preprint_collision: Above average as a process and it should be credited: dated re-scan (2026-09-03 over 2026-08-21), 15 HF queries, 244 papers, by-id verification of 54 IDs, a committed scan record with SHA256s, and — rare and to its credit — an explicit retraction of v2's claim that 'no published work uses one as the control for the other' after finding EvoAgentBench (2607.05202). But three things keep it from being a clean pass. First, the channel is demonstrably unreliable by the proposal's own admission: arXiv is unreachable from the node, verification runs through web-search snippets, and the August scan produced five false negatives (ActMem, MAS-PromptBench, TERMS-Bench, MemAPO, StructMemEval all exist) — a searcher with that false-negative rate cannot support a strong novelty claim, and the closest work is known only through a PDF supplied by the PI rather than a fetched source. Second, the check itself concedes the design primitive has never been searched: item (2) of the pre-freeze list is a targeted search for held-out-episode / data-provenance crossovers in prompt optimization and contamination work, i.e. the crossover that certifies the specificity probe is claimed novel without ever having been looked for. Own-vs-other-split transfer is a standard memorization/contamination move, and a collision there is likely. Third, the most damaging collision is not a hidden preprint but the one already cited: if EvoAgentBench really reports GEPA +1.2 vs ReasoningBank +3.6 on Qwen3.5-27B and GEPA +5.7 as the best automatic method on Gemma-4-31B, then 'an optimizer on the same episodes rivals the memory bank' is published, and this proposal is the careful follow-up measurement rather than the discovery. The residual-risk paragraph naming ICLR 2027 non-public submissions and NeurIPS 2026 camera-readies is realistic, and the re-scan commitment is the right mitigation, but as of the submitted text novelty rests on a search that has not covered one of the two design primitives.
